directions: Plant container-grown seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil with dappled shade from taller companion trees or shade cloth. Villa Sarchi is a naturally occurring dwarf mutation of Bourbon discovered near Sarchi, Costa Rica, valued for its compact, short-internode growth habit that allows closer spacing and easier hand-harvesting than taller arabica types. Keep soil evenly moist but never waterlogged, feed with a balanced fertilizer during the growing season, and protect from any temperature below 55°F. Expect the first modest harvest around three to four years after transplanting, with cherries ripening to a deep red.
sources: World Coffee Research Arabica Coffee Varieties Catalog
Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products

directions: Plant container-grown seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil beneath partial shade. San Ramon is a spontaneous dwarf mutation of Typica first identified in Brazil, prized for its very short internodes and stocky, bushy habit that makes it well suited to container culture or high-density plantings where space is limited. Water regularly to keep the root zone evenly moist, shelter from wind and any cold below 55°F, and fertilize lightly through the growing season to support steady leaf and branch development. Because of its compact size it is a popular choice for growers wanting an ornamental, fruit-bearing coffee plant in a greenhouse or large container.
sources: World Coffee Research Arabica Coffee Varieties Catalog
Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products

directions: Plant container-grown seedlings in spring in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil with light shade from taller trees. Java is a tall, vigorous arabica selection traced to Ethiopian and Yemeni stock introduced to the island of Java before being carried to Cameroon and later Central America, grown mainly for its notable tolerance of coffee leaf rust compared to older heirloom varieties. Give it more room than dwarf cultivars since it grows taller and more open, water deeply and regularly without letting the soil become soggy, and protect from any chill below 55°F. Prune lightly to maintain a manageable picking height in home or specialty plantings.
sources: World Coffee Research Arabica Coffee Varieties Catalog
Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products

directions: Plant seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil beneath the canopy of taller shade trees, mimicking the tree's native rainforest understory. Porcelana is a rare, pure Criollo strain from the Lake Maracaibo and Sierra de Perijá region of Venezuela, named for the pale, almost translucent ivory color of its beans and prized by fine chocolate makers for an unusually mild, delicate, low-tannin flavor. It is notably slow-growing, low-yielding, and highly susceptible to fungal disease, so it demands attentive humidity management, consistent warmth above 60°F, and protection from waterlogged soil. Expect a long wait of four to five years before the first meaningful harvest of pods.

Plant seedlings in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in the dappled shade of taller companion trees, replicating the sheltered coastal valley conditions of its origin. Chuao is a celebrated fine-flavor cacao of mixed Criollo-Trinitario ancestry grown almost exclusively in the isolated Chuao valley on Venezuela's Caribbean coast, where volcanic soils and a humid microclimate produce beans renowned among chocolate makers for their complex, fruity, low-bitterness character. Provide constant warmth above 60°F, high humidity, and shelter from wind, and expect several years of establishment before pods are produced in worthwhile quantity. This selection is a specialty planting for dedicated tropical fruit and chocolate enthusiasts rather than an easy home crop.

Plant rooted cuttings in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade, training the vine up a sturdy living or artificial support post. Panniyur-1 was released in 1961 by the Pepper Research Station in Panniyur, Kerala, India, as the first officially released high-yielding black pepper hybrid, valued for heavier fruit clusters and greater productivity than traditional local types. Maintain consistent humidity and warmth above 60°F year-round, water regularly without letting the root zone dry out, and provide light shade especially while the vine is young and establishing. Vines typically begin bearing three to four years after planting and continue producing for many years with proper support and fertility management.
sources: Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products

directions: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade, allowing the vine to climb a sturdy support post or living standard. Karimunda is the traditional, most widely grown black pepper cultivar across Kerala, India, favored by smallholders for its dependable moderate yields, broad soil adaptability, and relative tolerance of foot rot compared to many other selections. Keep the root zone consistently moist but never waterlogged, maintain warmth above 60°F with high ambient humidity, and mulch to conserve moisture between waterings. This adaptable, hardy standard is also commonly used as rootstock for grafting less vigorous but higher-quality pepper cultivars.
sources: Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered sun. Tieguanyin, meaning Iron Goddess of Mercy, is a renowned oolong tea cultivar that originated in Anxi County, Fujian Province, China, and is prized for producing a fragrant, floral, lingering oolong with a distinctive roasted or lightly fermented character depending on processing. It is somewhat less cold-hardy than northern Chinese or Japanese green tea cultivars, so it performs best in mild subtropical climates and appreciates consistent moisture and protection from harsh winter winds. Harvest the top two leaves and bud by hand for the finest quality, and prune into a rounded hedge shape after harvest flushes to encourage dense new growth.
sources: Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products

common_name: Jin Xuan Tea (Milk Oolong, TTES No. 12)
directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered sun. Jin Xuan, officially designated TTES No. 12, was bred by the Taiwan Tea Experiment Station and released in 1981, and is grown widely in Taiwan's mid- and high-elevation gardens for its naturally creamy, sweet aroma that gives rise to the popular 'milk oolong' style. It is a vigorous, disease-tolerant cultivar that adapts well to a range of elevations but still needs protection from hard freezes and benefits from steady soil moisture during the growing season. Pick the youngest leaves and bud for oolong processing, and shape the shrub into a low hedge to make hand or mechanical harvesting easier.
sources: Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plant Products
